text:
Predicates:
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
AppearsInCompanyToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
RemoteFromHome(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in another country.
James ::: James is a specific individual.

Premises:
∀x (SchedulesMeeting(x, y) → AppearsInCompanyToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → SchedulesMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountry(x) → RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: All employees in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
James ::: James is a specific individual.
(Manager(james) ∧ AppearsInCompanyToday(james)) ∨ ¬(Manager(james) ∨ AppearsInCompanyToday(james)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.

Conclusion:
∃x (LunchInCompany(x) ∧ x = james) ::: James has lunch in the company.
